1 · Intro

When to use it.

HCMs don't run payroll. Payroll runs payroll. Your job is getting records and time cards right so payroll can run cleanly.

This course covers what you own and what payroll owns, the pay rules that change non-exempt pay, which paycheck a change will hit, and the errors that most often cause a late or wrong paycheck.

Use this whenYou are new to the HCM role, you are not sure whether a pay issue is yours, or you want to check your work before a cutoff.

2 · Walk through

Your role, the rules, how a change pays, and the errors to catch.

Check off each item as you read.

Which paycheck will it hit?
SituationTypical result
Approved before cutoff, effective this periodPaid this period
Approved after cutoff, effective this periodPaid next period with retro
Effective date in a past, paid periodRetro difference paid in a later run
Hourly rate change, non-exemptApplies to approved UKG hours in the period

Watch-outs

  • HCMs can't run or rerun payroll. That is payroll's job.
  • Open item: Payroll is still documenting which payroll elements you should confirm on the record at hire.
  • Open item: confirm whether line managers or HCMs keep up with late and missing time cards, since payroll usually notifies the line manager.
  • These are the federal rules. A state where the employee works can require more.
  • Never remove or reduce hours an employee worked to avoid overtime.
  • Open item: Vanderbilt's rule on whether paid time off and holidays count toward overtime, and which seven days make the overtime workweek. The published calendar shows weekly pay periods running Monday to Sunday and biweekly periods Sunday to Saturday.
  • Open item: Vanderbilt's holiday pay rules, shift differential rates, on-call and call-back pay, and the UKG pay code for each. Payroll is documenting these.
  • Pending approvals do not pay. A change still waiting in approvals at cutoff misses that payroll.
  • Retro only covers elements set up for retroactive pay. Do not promise a retro amount; payroll calculates it.
  • Open item: confirm with payroll which Vanderbilt earnings use Process separately and how retro shows on the payslip.
  • Close to the payroll deadline, you can email payroll and ask them to put a payment on their watch list.
  • Fixes after payroll runs become retro adjustments in a later payroll and may mean a late or incorrect paycheck.
  • If you find one of these after payroll has run, bring payroll the facts. Do not try to correct the pay yourself.
  • Open item: Payroll to supply the errors it corrects most often, with counts, so this list can be ranked and kept current.

Q6A manager asks whether working a holiday is automatically overtime. What do you say?

HCM Academy job aid · Payroll & Timecards

Payroll essentials: your role, pay rules, and common errors

Use when: You are new to the HCM role, you are not sure whether a pay issue is yours, or you want to check your work before a cutoff. · System: Overview

  1. All new hires: you own the hire.
    • Process the hire correctly.
    • Confirm every payroll element is on the record.
  2. Exempt (monthly) staff: hands off, with two exceptions.
    • Add a compensation payment when needed, such as a lump sum.
    • Work an issue with payroll when one comes up.
  3. Weekly and biweekly employees: check time cards every week.
    • Confirm every time card is submitted.
    • Follow up with line managers on missing or late time cards.
    • Payroll usually notifies the line manager when a time card isn't approved.
    • Escalate errors you can't resolve to payroll.
  4. Errors: you fix them, and work with payroll when you need more information.
  5. Start with who the rules apply to.
  6. Overtime: more than 40 hours worked in a workweek.
    • Over 40 hours worked in the workweek: overtime.
    • Weekend or holiday work by itself: not overtime under federal law.
  7. Count each workweek on its own.
  8. Count hours worked, not hours paid.
  9. Holidays: paid by policy, not by federal law.
  10. Shift differentials: paid by policy, and they raise the overtime rate.
  11. On-call time: it depends on how free the employee is.
    • Required to stay at the work site: hours worked.
    • At home and free to use the time: generally not hours worked.
    • Called in to work: the time spent working counts.
  12. Unapproved overtime still gets paid.
  13. Check the time card, then ask payroll.
  14. The salary basis decides how pay is stored.
  15. Saving a salary change writes the person's element entry.
  16. The effective date says when the pay is earned; the cutoff says when it is paid.
    • Check the payroll calendar, not memory
  17. Backdated changes pay through retroactive processing.
  18. Some earnings are set to Process separately.
  19. Confirm the result before payday.
  20. Check costing with every pay change.
  21. A paid person set to Active no payroll.
  22. A change still pending at the cutoff.
  23. The wrong effective date.
  24. Amount and Net mixed up on a one-time payment.
  25. A supplement that never ends.
  26. Hours changed without the salary, or the salary without the hours.
  27. A missing or unapproved time card.
  28. Terminate Employment used when the person keeps another job.
  29. Costing left as it was after a move.
  30. A wrong value on a position.
